Senses.Explanation: Literally "hand over, entrust" (付) the "teaching" (法): "entrust the teaching," attested 608 times in 143 allowlisted texts. Lamp records use it for a named predecessor handing the teaching to a successor: "after the buddha's extinction, the teaching was entrusted to Kasyapa and mind was transmitted by mind" (佛滅後付法於迦葉，以心傳心). Narrative closure frequently says "after the patriarch had entrusted the teaching" (祖付法已), followed by his departure or death. The compound "verse on entrusting the teaching" (付法偈) names verses spoken or recorded at that handover.
Senses.Note: The verses themselves often question the wording of transmission. One early verse says, "originally a teaching was entrusted; after entrusting it, [one] says there is no teaching; each must awaken for oneself; once awakened, there is no no-teaching" (本來付有法，付了言無法，各各須自悟，悟了無無法). A later preface asks why transmission verses are recorded for earlier buddhas and patriarchs but not below Mazu: was there no entrustment, or was it kept from disclosure? Another instruction ranks a thousand who have opened up below one person entrusted with the teaching, and a thousand entrusted below one who goes out into the world. These are text-stated comparisons within the same verb sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又佛滅後付法於迦葉，以心傳心
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An Ancestral Hall question states that after the buddha's extinction, the teaching was entrusted to Kasyapa and mind transmitted by mind.

Occurrences.Kwic: 從上佛祖皆見有付法偈
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A preface reports the claim that buddhas and patriarchs from earlier times all have verses on entrusting the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 本來付有法付了言無法各各須自悟悟了無無法阿難付法眼藏竟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Early transmission verse: originally a teaching was entrusted; after entrusting it, one says there is no teaching; each must awaken for oneself. The narrative then says Ananda finished entrusting the eye-treasury of the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖付法已。即現神變而入涅槃。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Lamp narrative closure: after the patriarch entrusted the teaching, he manifested transformations and entered extinction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 千個省發者不如一付法者，千個付法者不如一出世者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A letter ranks a thousand who have opened up below one entrusted with the teaching, and a thousand entrusted below one who goes out into the world.

Senses.Explanation: The first graph means “investigate, interrogate, or put to the test” (勘); the second means “break open or expose” (破). (勘破) is what a master does in a live encounter: he tests someone and sees through them. The stock capping declaration (勘破了也) ('[I have] seen him through') marks the testing as complete. The paradigm case is Zhaozhou, who hears of an old woman on the road to Mt. Wutai who answers every pilgrim's question with '(just) go straight on'; he goes up to test her (待我去勘過), comes back, and tells the monk (臺山婆子為汝勘破了也) ('I have seen the Mt. Wutai crone through for you'). Commentators then keep the word working by asking (什麼處是勘破處) ('and just where is the point where she got seen through?'). The verb is also turned reflexively: Dahui says to a monk (老僧被爾勘破) ('this old monk has been seen through by you') and, when the monk hesitates, hits him. In the (無門關) (the Gateless Barrier) the word both titles and closes cases: its case-table lists (趙州勘婆) ('Zhaozhou tests the crone'), the case itself ends (州歸謂眾曰)。(臺山婆子我與爾勘破了也), Wumen's comment turns the word into the probe (且道那裏是趙州勘破婆子處) ('say then: just where is the place Zhaozhou saw the crone through?'), and on the two-hermits case (州勘庵主) he writes (爭奈趙州却被二庵主勘破) ('but alas, Zhaozhou was himself seen through by the two hermits') — the tester can be out-tested. The probe form recurs in raised-case commentary: (老宿拈云)。(什麼處是勘破處) ('an old worthy took it up: where is the seeing-through point?'). The preliminary step has its own verb (勘過) ('go and test'): Zhaozhou announces (待我去勘過) ('wait till I go test her'), and Xuansha counters Xuefeng's praise of a student's verse (此子徹去也, 'this one has broken through') with (未可)。(此是意識著述)。(更須勘過始得) ('not yet — this is composition by the conceptual mind; he must still be tested').
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense; no master bends the word idiosyncratically. (勘破) is also used of 'seeing through' a case (公案) or checkpoint, but the defining Zen use is person-to-person testing. The Mt. Wutai crone case recurs verbatim across lamp records (燈錄), case-commentary, and recorded sayings (語錄), which is what makes the reading multi-source. Counts (462-text allowlist grep): (勘破) 1503 hits in 253 texts; the verdict formula (勘破了也) 241 in 118; the passive (被我勘破) 23 in 18; the commentators' probe (勘破處) 51 in 38 (什麼處是勘破處 7 hits in 7 texts, e.g. 老宿拈云。什麼處是勘破處 T47n1997 0804b28; 甚麼處是勘破處 2); the preliminary verb (勘過) 296 in 129 (待我去勘過 X80n1565 0092b11; 更須勘過始得 X80n1565 0152c22); the sibling term (勘辨) 171 in 77. (無門關) material: case-table (趙州勘婆) T48n2005 0292c06; (臺山婆子我與爾勘破了也) 0297a13; (且道那裏是趙州勘破婆子處) 0297a17; (爭奈趙州却被二庵主勘破) 0294b14.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師歸院謂僧曰。臺山婆子為汝勘破了也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Section head is (趙州觀音院從諗禪師); (師) = Zhaozhou, returning to tell the monk he has seen the Mt. Wutai woman through. (Wudeng Huiyuan, a lamp record 燈錄.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪竇著語云。勘破了也。一似鐵橛相似。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Xuedou's capping phrase (著語) on the Deshan-visits-Guishan case; Yuanwu's commentary then asks (什麼處是勘破處) / (且道勘破德山勘破溈山). (Blue Cliff Record.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 萬松道。勘破了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong's own capping ('萬松道。勘破了也') on the same Mt. Wutai woman case, adding the reflexive twist (亦乃累及萬松) ('it even implicates Wansong'). (Book of Serenity.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。老僧被爾勘破。僧擬議。師便打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (師) = Dahui in his own recorded encounter; the inverted use — the master says HE has been seen through, then strikes. (Dahui's recorded sayings 語錄.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 州歸院云。婆子被我勘破了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The line (婆子被我勘破了也) is Zhaozhou's (州), here raised and commented on ('趙州不施韜略...又却失利') in Xutang Zhiyu's yulu — an independent witness to the stock phrase.

Senses.Explanation: As a verb, "to examine and discriminate" (勘辨) joins "to examine or interrogate" (勘) with "to discriminate or distinguish" (辨). Chan records use it for testing interlocutors and claims in the public record. One master says that after examination and discrimination are clear and the matter is firmly grasped, activity in the dusty net is unobstructed; another record rebukes a man who claimed he could examine masters everywhere; Xutang says, "I too cannot examine and discriminate you," and contrasts an amicable one-question, one-answer meeting with having "so much examination and discrimination." The Chan deviation lies in its institutional object: this legal-investigative wording names how masters question, check, and distinguish people and their answers.
Senses.Note: 170 occurrences in 78 allowlisted texts across verbal use and section/genre headings. Split under depth-gate item 8 because the corpus also uses the same graphs as the name of a record section.

Occurrences.Kwic: 勘辨既明，把捉既定，却不妨向塵勞世網中大抹高揮
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The text says, "once examination and discrimination are clear, once grasping is settled..."

Occurrences.Kwic: 真點胸自謂百了千當，勘辨諸方
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The record says Zhen Dianxiong claimed complete competence and examined masters in every quarter; the following exchange tests that claim.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我也不能勘辨得爾。只要諸人知道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Xutang says, "I too cannot examine and discriminate you; I only want all of you to know."

Occurrences.Kwic: 當時勘辨諸方底手眼向甚處去？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public address asks where the capacity formerly used to examine masters in every quarter has gone.

Senses.Explanation: As a record heading, "examinations and discriminations" names a collected section of encounter dialogues. The Old Records of the Venerable Ones places the heading immediately before Huangbo's kitchen exchange with the rice steward. Later recorded-sayings tables of contents coordinate it with "posed questions, question-and-answer, and occasions of encounter" and divide the material across volumes. Here the graphs denote a textual category containing public exchanges, rather than the finite verb "to examine someone."
Senses.Note: This noun/genre use is anchored separately because it denotes a section of a record, not merely another interpretation of the verbal act.

Occurrences.Kwic: 勘辨勘辨黃檗因入厨次問飯頭作什麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The duplicated section heading "examinations and discriminations" immediately precedes Huangbo's question to the rice steward.

Occurrences.Kwic: 第十六卷垂問勘辨問答機緣上第十七卷勘辨問答機緣下
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The table of contents labels volumes 16–17 "posed questions, examinations and discriminations, question-and-answer, and occasions of encounter."

Senses.Explanation: A phonetic name for the Vinaya, the body of binding monastic rules. The term occurs 190 times in 88 allowlisted texts. Chan records retain that hard-rule sense but deploy it across biography, institutional teaching, admonition, and public comparison. A biographical passage records Nanyue Huairang studying the Vinaya treasury before going to Caoqi. A later monastic admonition calls its detailed rules restraints on beginners and says the speaker never attended a Vinaya teaching seat. Sanfeng says that the preceptor expounds Vinaya in the morning while he addresses the assembly in the evening, then assigns immeasurable fault to both if this is discussed as the buddha teaching. Dahui juxtaposes Danxia's burning of a wooden buddha, which 'did not comply with human sentiment,' with Cuiwei's offering to the arhats, which 'accorded with Vinaya according to circumstances' (隨方毘尼), then says neither is usable at his gate. Thus the word names a rule corpus and its institutional study and teaching; Chan masters also place that institution inside their own recorded comparisons rather than giving it one uniform verdict.
Senses.Note: The Sanskrit-derived name is translated here by its attested institutional function. The cited passages record study, detailed restraints, and contrasting public uses; they do not state one uniform verdict on the rules.

Occurrences.Kwic: 丹霞燒木佛。不順人情。翠微供羅漢。隨方毘尼。若到徑山門下。總用不著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui places 'accorded with Vinaya according to circumstances' beside Danxia and Cuiwei, then says both are unusable at his own gate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 依弘景律師出家通天二年受戒後習毘尼藏一日自嘆曰夫出家者為無為法
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A biographical witness records ordination followed by study of the Vinaya treasury.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛先制律。啟創發蒙軌則威儀。淨如氷雪。止持作犯束斂初心。微細條章革諸猥弊。毘尼法席曾未叨陪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monastic admonition explicitly links Vinaya with rules, deportment, prohibitions, requirements, infractions, and detailed clauses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三峰院裏日逐事生，闍黎朝演毘尼，老僧晚參示眾。若作佛法商量，我也沒量罪過，你也沒量罪過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sanfeng distinguishes the preceptor's morning Vinaya exposition from his evening address, then rebukes treating either as material for discussing the buddha teaching.

AlternateTargets: stand at the top of the high peak
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "stand atop the high, high peak." The phrase occurs 55 times in 38 allowlisted texts. It is overwhelmingly paired with "walk on the floor of the deepest sea" (深深海底行). In a recorded biography, Zhaojue asks a student, "stand atop the highest peak; walk on the floor of the deepest sea—how do you understand it?" The student awakens at the words and says, "my heels are nailed fast" (釘殺脚跟也); Zhaojue then raises the whisk and asks another question. The paired line also serves as a direct answer in public interview and as an instruction to an assembly: "at this point it is just right to stand atop the highest peak and walk on the floor of the deepest sea" (到恁麼地，正好高高峰頂立，深深海底行). Another address distributes the pair across dates: before the twenty-fifth, the ocean-floor line; after it, the summit line; on the twenty-fifth, all ten directions cut off. Zen turns impossible vertical extremes into a fixed paired demand, question, answer, and biographical exchange; the corpus does not require this entry to decode the image further.
Senses.Note: The summit half is retained as its own headword because it recurs independently, but its dominant corpus relation is the sea-floor half. Question, answer, instruction, and date-pairing all use the same spatial action; they do not warrant multiple senses. The biography names a student's awakening at the question but does not define the phrase as awakening itself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 覺一日問師：高高峰頂立，深深海底行。汝作麼生會？師于言下頓悟曰：釘殺脚跟也。覺拈起拂子曰：這箇又作麼生？師一笑而出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhaojue asks how the student understands the paired line; the biography records awakening at the words, an answer about nailed heels, and a follow-up with the whisk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸仁者！到恁麼地，正好高高峰頂立，深深海底行，
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An assembly is told that at this point it is just right to stand atop the highest peak and walk on the deepest sea floor.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「高高峰頂立，深深海底行。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The complete paired line is delivered as an answer in a public exchange.

Occurrences.Kwic: 二十五日已前，虛空包不住，深深海底行；二十五日已後，大地載不起，高高峰頂立；正當二十五日，十方俱坐斷，縱橫得自由。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address assigns the sea-floor half before the twenty-fifth, the summit half after it, and a third line to the day itself.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, "silent" or "wordless" (默) and "illumination" or "illuminate" (照): "silent illumination," attested 113 times in 61 allowlisted texts. The corpus does not give it one uniformly approved category. Hongzhi says, "one who knows the sound discerns; one of silent illumination is numinous" (知音者鑑，默照者神), and elsewhere writes "at the place of silently illuminating, the sky is clear in autumn" (默默照處天宇澄秋). Dahui uses the same compound critically. He calls certain recent people in the monasteries "those called silent illumination" (謂之默照者), says "although silent illumination is not permitted, everyone must face the wall" (雖然不許默照，須要人人面壁), and lamp witnesses report his phrase "followers of silent illumination sit year after year in a ghost cave" (默照之徒，鬼窟長年打坐). A later Sanfeng record supplies a direct naming formula and rejects what it names: "if while sitting one illuminates something bright and numinous and takes it as oneself, this is called silent-illumination Chan" (若坐中照得昭昭靈靈為自己者，謂之默照禪), followed immediately by the author's adverse classification. Thus the entry preserves Hongzhi's affirmative compound, Dahui's explicit opposition, and the later critical definition as a contested Chinese term.
Senses.Note: Corpus collocations: "silent-illumination Chan" (默照禪), 5; "followers of silent illumination" (默照之徒), 12; "silent illumination is not permitted" (不許默照), 2; "withered Chan and silent illumination" (枯禪默照), 6; "oppose silent illumination" (排默照), 14; "at the place of silently illuminating" (默默照處), 1. These counts show both self-description and sustained criticism in the Chinese record.

Occurrences.Kwic: 知音者鑑。默照者神。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hongzhi's formal address: "one who knows the sound discerns; one of silent illumination is numinous."

Occurrences.Kwic: 近日叢林無鼻孔輩。謂之默照者。是也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's reply to Professor Yan: "the recent noseless lot in the monasteries—these are those called silent illumination." This is overt criticism.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然不許默照。須要人人面壁。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's formal address: "although silent illumination is not permitted, everyone must face the wall."

Occurrences.Kwic: 致令默照之徒，鬼窟長年打坐。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui's section of the Orthodox Continuation of the Lamps: "causing followers of silent illumination to sit year after year in a ghost cave."

Occurrences.Kwic: 若坐中照得昭昭靈靈為自己者，謂之默照禪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Direct naming formula in the Sanfeng record: "if while sitting one illuminates something bright and numinous and takes it as oneself, this is called silent-illumination Chan." The author immediately rejects the named category; no roster link is set.
